Two moles each of the gases \(P_2, Q_2\) and PQ are present in a vessel at equilibrium. If 1 mole each of \(P_2\) and \(Q_2\) is added at equilibrium, then determine the composition (in mole) of each species at the new equilibrium ?

1. \(\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{P}_2}=0.5, \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{Q}_2}=0.5, \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{PQ}}=1 \)
2. \(\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{P}_2}=1.33, \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{Q}_2}=1.33, \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{PQ}}=1.67\)
3. \(\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{P}_2}=2.67, \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{O}_2}=2.67, \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{PQ}}=2.33 \)
4. \(\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{P}_2}=2.67, \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{Q}_2}=2.67, \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{PQ}}=2.67\)

At \(\mathrm{298~K},\) The equilibrium constant is \(2 \times10^{15}\) for the reaction: \(\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{s})+2 \mathrm{Ag}^{+}(\mathrm{aq}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{Cu}^{2+}(\mathrm{aq})+2 \mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{s})\).
If the equilibrium constant for the reaction \(\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{Cu}^{2+}(\mathrm{aq})+\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{s}) \rightleftharpoons \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{s})+\mathrm{Ag}^{+}(\mathrm{aq})\) is \(x \times 10^{-8}\), then find the value of \(\mathrm{x}\) in nearest integer form:

1. Eight (8)
2. Five (5)
3. Six (6)
4. Two (2)
questions.explanation:
Hint:The second reaction is just reversed and halved form of the first reaction. Explanation: \(\begin{aligned} &\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{s})+2 \mathrm{Ag}^{+}(\mathrm{aq}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{Cu}^{2+}(\mathrm{aq})+2 \mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{s}) \\ & \mathrm{k}=2 \times 10^{15} \\ & \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{s})+\mathrm{Ag}^{+}(\mathrm{aq}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{Cu}^{+2}(\mathrm{aq})+2 \mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{s}) \end{aligned}\\ &\begin{aligned} \mathrm{K}^{\prime}=\frac{1}{(\mathrm{~K})^{1 / 2}} & =\frac{1}{\left(2 \times 10^{15}\right)^{1 / 2}} \\ & =2.23 \times 10^{-8} \end{aligned} \end{aligned}\) Therefore,\(\mathrm{x=2}\)is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Which of the following is true for the degree of dissociation \(\alpha\) and pressure \(\mathrm{{P}_{T}}, \) for the reversible reaction \(\mathrm{{A}({g})} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{{B}({g})+{C}({g})} \)?
1. If \(\mathrm{{P}_{T} \gg K_{P}},\) then \(\alpha \approx 1 \)
2. If \(\mathrm{{P}_{T}}\) increases, then \(\alpha\) decreases
3. If \(\mathrm{{P}_{T}}\) increases, then \(\alpha\) increases
4. If \(\mathrm{K_P \gg P_T,} \) then \(\alpha \) tends towards 0
questions.explanation:
Hint: Le Chatelier's Principle Explanation:According to Le Chatelier's Principle, if you increase the total pressure (\(P_T\)​), the equilibrium will shift to the side with fewer moles of gas to relieve the stress. This means the equilibrium shifts to the left (backward reaction), which consumes B and C to form A. A shift to the left means the degree of dissociation (α) must decrease. Thus, second statement is CORRECT. The expression for \(K_P\) is: \(K_P=\frac{P_B P_C}{P_A}=\frac{\left(\frac{\alpha}{1+\alpha} \cdot P_T\right) \cdot\left(\frac{\alpha}{1+\alpha} \cdot P_T\right)}{\frac{1-\alpha}{1+\alpha} \cdot P_T}=\frac{\frac{\alpha^2 P_T^2}{(1+\alpha)^2}}{\frac{1-\alpha}{1+\alpha} \cdot P_T}=\frac{\alpha^2 P_T^2}{(1+\alpha)^2} \cdot \frac{1+\alpha}{(1-\alpha) P_T}=\frac{\alpha^2 P_T}{(1-\alpha)(1+\alpha)}\) Simplifying, we get: \(K_P=\frac{\alpha^2 P_T}{1-\alpha^2}\) Analysis of Each Option: 1. If \(P_T \gg K_P,\) then \(\alpha \approx 1\) * From \(K_P=\frac{\alpha^2 P_T}{1-\alpha^2},\) if \(P_T \gg K_P,\) the equation suggests that for \(\alpha\) to be large (close to \(1\) ), the denominator \(1-\alpha^2\) must be small, but this would require \(K_P\) to be very large as well, which contradicts \(P_T \gg K_P.\) In reality, high \(P_T\) favors the reactant side (lower \(\alpha\) ) due to the increase in moles on the product side. Thus, \(\alpha \approx 1\) is unlikely when \(P_T \gg K_P.\) This statement is 2.
